House · Easy

Alert Limit: 10 · Loot: Crumb/Trinket · For: a first session

The Objective

A specific cookie — the good kind, from the tin with the blue lid — in the kitchen of a single-story house. In and out. Except the cat is new.

What the Crew Sees at the Score

A standard two-bedroom home. The objective is a tin on the second shelf of the cabinet just past the end of the counter. In plain sight: a young cat, very interested in things, and a human who gets up for water during the night. Two ways in: the wall vent, or up through the sink's drain.

Present only what's visible. The intel, the threats, and the unknown obstacle are ST information — let Planning reveal the rest.

The kitchen. A: the wall vent. B: the sink drain, a squeeze (Chapter 3). Red paw: the cat's bed. The counter top is 3 squares up; the tin's shelf is 5. The doorway leads to the hall, the bathroom and the bedrooms. Storyteller's copy: anything dashed in red is the unknown obstacle — keep it off what the crew sees.

One square = one spider. Gold letters are entry points, red tokens are where threats start, numbered circles are the Suggested Obstacles, and E1/E2 lie on the dashed gold escape route.

Intel the crew can uncover by Casing — one true detail per Success, and never more than this list (extra Successes buy nothing; Casing never reveals the unknown obstacle):

  • The counter and the cabinet were wiped down this evening and are slippery (Acrobatics to climb).
  • The cat's bed is 9 squares from the cabinet.
  • The human's water runs roughly every ninety minutes.
  • The bottle cap on the floor is exactly the kind of shiny thing the cat can't ignore.

Asleep down the hall (a Sleeping Human, Chapter 15). A heist doesn't last ninety minutes, so the next water run only comes early: when the Alert reaches 7, or at once on a Mid-Heist Complication of 3 (Chapter 20). They take 2 rounds to reach the sink, fill a glass for 1, and go back to bed. While they're in the kitchen the lights are on, and Stealth against them is Difficulty 2.

ST information. Don't foreshadow it in the Score — let it arrive.

There are two identical tins on that shelf. One holds cookies. One holds sewing supplies. The crew finds out which the hard way. Before play, roll a d6 in secret: 1–3, the cookies are in the left tin; 4–6, the right. From outside, only a nose can tell them apart.

Roll it now: [[/gmr 1d6]]{Which tin? 1–3 left, 4–6 right}

Obstacles 1–4 are the heist: each takes two successful rolls (Partial or better), and a group check counts as both. E1 and E2 are the suggested Escape obstacles: one successful roll each, and at least one of them never needs Athletics. Difficulties are for a calm location; the Alert raises them. Opposed means the creature rolls first, and its Successes + 1 are your Difficulty.

#ObstacleRoll (Difficulty)
1Cross the kitchen floor while the cat is awake and watching the door. Awake means active and roaming from the start: +1 Alert each round, wherever the crew is (Chapter 9). From the drain, the wet counter top costs double movement.Stealth, opposed (its Perception 4) · charm it: Persuasion, opposed · flick the bottle cap past it, its Weakness: Athletics (1)
2Climb the cabinet — slippery surface, freshly wiped.Acrobatics (1), +1 for the height (Chapter 3); a Silk Line takes 1 off
3Open the tin quietly. Tight lid. The Tinkerer will have opinions.Engineering (3) · force it: Athletics (3), and the lid pops: +1 Alert
4(Unknown) It's the sewing tin. The cookies are in its twin, right beside it. Recalibrate.Sniff out the butter first: Perception (4) · open the twin: as obstacle 3
E1Back across with the cookie, the cat still watching.Stealth, opposed (the cat) · one spider times its head-turns for everyone: Tactics (3)
E2It's the good kind of cookie: crumbly. And the way out is a squeeze.Wrap it in silk first: Engineering (2) · ease it through: Acrobatics (2) · or shove it and leave the crumbs: incomplete loot (Chapter 11)
